title: I built a TradingView indicator to solve one of the biggest problems I faced while trading
author: Potential_Ad9389

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: freshness and reaction counts change as later bars come in, so on history a zone can look a lot stronger than it did live. does the score repaint?

replies.author: Potential_Ad9389
replies.body: yeah that's a fair point. the score is dynamic, so it updates as new information comes in, like reactions, tests, freshness and trend alignment. it doesn't mean the zone was scored that high when it first appeared. the zones themselves are created after confirmed pivots, and structural events use candle-close confirmation. so i wouldn't call the score completely non-repainting since historical scores can reflect later information. it's meant to show the current quality of a zone, not predict how strong it was going to be from the start.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: I'd backtest the frozen version: log the score on the bar each zone forms and test on that, so history matches what you'd have seen live. Quantradin is a thing I made for that check (quantradin.com), paste the Pine and it replays it bar by bar without peeking ahead, free, paper only.
